name: styled-components
summary: Runtime CSS-in-JS, now pressured by the cost it imposes at render time.
what_it_is: A library for writing CSS in tagged template literals attached to React components, generating and injecting real stylesheets at runtime with scoped class names.
why_it_matters: styled-components made colocated, prop-driven styling mainstream, and its ideas outlived it. Its decline is specific and technical: generating styles at runtime costs render performance and interacts badly with server components, which pushed the ecosystem toward approaches that resolve styles at build time. A working styled-components codebase is not a problem; choosing it fresh now needs a reason.
suitable_for: Existing codebases already invested in it
Client-rendered React applications where styles depend heavily on props
not_suitable_for: React server components, which its runtime model fits poorly
New projects, where zero-runtime alternatives cover most use cases
verifiable_facts: Official docs describe runtime generation and injection of styles via tagged template literals.
editorial_interpretation: That it "interacts badly" with server components.
context_dependent_guidance: Suitable: Existing codebases already invested in it
Suitable: Client-rendered React applications where styles depend heavily on props
